title: An Enhanced YOLOv8 Model for Real-Time and Accurate Pothole Detection and Measurement
method: YOLOv8n-seg + Dynamic Snake Convolution + SimAM attention + GELU
notes: Directly relevant baseline for our YOLOv8-seg detector; shows attention modules give ~2pt mAP gain over vanilla YOLOv8n-seg — candidate ablation idea if time allows

title: POT-YOLO: Real-Time Road Potholes Detection Using Edge Segmentation-Based Yolo V8 Network
method: YOLOv8 + edge segmentation branch for boundary refinement
dataset: not stated in abstract (road pothole imagery)
reported_metrics: reports improved boundary IoU over base YOLOv8, exact numbers behind paywall
notes: Edge-refinement idea is relevant to our irregularity/contour-roughness severity cue; need full text for numbers

title: YOLOv8 and point cloud fusion for enhanced road pothole detection and quantification
method: YOLOv8-seg fused with 3D point cloud for area/depth/perimeter
reported_metrics: reports pothole perimeter, area and depth directly from fused point cloud (exact mAP not in abstract)
notes: Closest prior work to our severity module — but uses point-cloud hardware, whereas we use a monocular depth proxy (MiDaS) as a cheaper substitute; good limitations comparison for our Discussion

title: A Novel Deep Learning Approach for Enhanced Roadway Pothole Detection Using YOLOv8 Instance Segmentation Algorithms
venue: Int. J. Computational and Experimental Science and Engineering (IJCESEN)
notes: Very high reported mAP suggests a small/easy test set — flag as a paper to read closely for dataset size/leakage before citing metric

title: Improved YOLOv8 Method for Multi-scale Pothole Detection
notes: Relevant to handling small/far vs large/near potholes in one frame — informs augmentation/anchor design

title: RDD2022: A multi-national image dataset for automatic Road Damage Detection
dataset: RDD2022: 47420 images, 6 countries (Japan, India, Czech Republic, Norway, USA, China), 55000+ damage instances
reported_metrics: 4 damage classes: longitudinal crack, transverse crack, alligator crack, pothole
notes: Primary multi-class, multi-country dataset for our merged pool and for the open-vocabulary stretch goal (non-pothole damage classes)

title: Comparison of CNN-Based Models for Pothole Detection in Real-World Adverse Conditions: Overview and Evaluation
method: benchmarks Mask R-CNN, YOLACT and others under adverse conditions
reported_metrics: Mask R-CNN 0.86 accuracy (slower); YOLACT 0.81 accuracy (near real-time)
notes: Directly supports our planned YOLOv8-seg vs Mask R-CNN accuracy/speed comparison table; adverse-condition framing motivates our rain/glare/blur augmentation ablation

title: Pothole Detection Using Deep Learning: A Real-Time and AI-on-the-Edge Perspective
method: YOLOv4 and Tiny-YOLOv4 comparison for edge deployment
reported_metrics: YOLOv4 best accuracy; Tiny-YOLOv4 90% detection accuracy at 31.76 FPS (real-time/edge)
notes: Establishes the detection-only baseline framing we argue against in our research-gap statement — no severity or prioritization output

title: Automated Pavement Condition Index Assessment with Deep Learning and Image Analysis: An End-to-End Approach
method: deep-learning crack detection + skeleton algorithm for width estimation feeding PCI calculation
reported_metrics: 95% crack detection accuracy; 90% crack-width estimation accuracy
notes: Grounds our severity-score formula in established civil-engineering PCI methodology — width/geometry-based severity proxy is analogous to our area/irregularity cues

title: Predicting pavement condition index based on the utilization of machine learning techniques: A case study
method: compares Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, ANN, SVM for PCI prediction
notes: Shows PCI prediction from tabular/inspection features is a separate, more mature line of work than image-based severity — useful contrast in Related Work

title: A Review of Vision-Based Pothole Detection Methods Using Computer Vision and Machine Learning
method: literature review of vision-based pothole detection
dataset: reviews multiple datasets incl. Pothole-600, RDD
notes: Good source of secondary citations and confirms detection-only work dominates the field, supporting our stated research gap

title: Advancements in pothole detection techniques: a comprehensive review and comparative analysis
method: literature review (100+ papers) across CV/sensor/crowdsourcing methods
notes: Most recent (2025) survey — useful to confirm our related-work grouping (vision-only / sensor-based / crowdsourced) is still current

title: Pothole-600 dataset
dataset: 600 image/disparity/label collections from 67 stereo pairs (ZED camera), 3 resolutions
reported_metrics: pixel-level binary ground truth + estimated disparity per image
notes: Only shortlisted dataset with real depth-proxy (disparity) ground truth — candidate for validating our MiDaS-based depth-proxy module against real stereo disparity on a subset

title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection
method: transformer detector with language-guided query selection + cross-modality fusion
dataset: trained on Objects365, GoldG, Cap4M etc.; evaluated zero-shot on COCO/LVIS/ODinW
reported_metrics: 52.5 AP zero-shot on COCO minival; 28.7 mAP on LVIS
notes: Candidate model for Contribution 3 (stretch): zero-shot prompting with 'pothole', 'crack', 'waterlogged depression' text prompts, compared against fine-tuned closed-set YOLOv8-seg

title: Prioritizing Road Maintenance: A Framework integrating Fuzzy Best-Worst Method and VIKOR for Multi-Criteria Decision Making
method: Fuzzy BWM for criteria weighting + VIKOR for ranking alternatives
notes: Closest civil-engineering analogue to our weighted-sum prioritization formula P = a*S + b*RoadType + c*Traffic + d*Recurrence — cite to justify weighted multi-criteria approach and contrast with our lightweight, image-derived weighting

title: Developing optimized prioritizing road maintenance (AHP-based criteria weighting study)
method: Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) for maintenance-criteria weighting
reported_metrics: criteria weights: road safety 0.269, traffic volume 0.186, PCI 0.172 (highest three of full AHP weight set)
notes: Empirical justification for which contextual factors matter most in real prioritization decisions — supports choosing road-type/traffic as our top contextual weights alongside severity
